dedupe_keys.name: philippines optimising primary care facility locations for universal health care with a cooperative covering model

description: This case study applies a facility location model to decide where to place primary care facilities in a Philippine city, where site selection has usually followed political and pragmatic considerations. The authors, from the Philippine Institute for Development Studies, published it as an open-access journal article. They proposed a variant of cooperative maximal covering models with parameters for equity and efficiency and demonstrated it on an actual city using open source data such as population, road networks and existing facility locations. Coverage is one Philippine city. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the model uses open data of varying quality, results depend on the chosen coverage radius and weights, and it demonstrates feasibility, not an adopted plan. The study generated multiple candidate primary care sites depending on the equity and efficiency parameters and argues the approach can support evidence-based, multi-criterion facility location decisions by government and other sectors. Simulation uses: a worked example of optimisation for healthcare capacity planning, adaptable to include hazard exposure constraints. Related records: AccessMod (model-accessmod) computes geographic accessibility for such analyses and WorldPop (data-worldpop-global-gridded-population) supplies population inputs.
